title: PIRIN EXTREME 38K - race day
terrain: 38.1km, 3440m D+ (GPX). Km 0-13: climb 923->2908m (Vihren). Km 13-28: traverse above 2000m, 9.7km above 2500m. Km 28-38: one 1250m descent to Bansko

steps.target: Z2, opening 1900m climb - hike, strictly conversational
Z2-Z3, high traverse - effort not pace, air is thin
Z2, final 1250m descent - controlled, short stride

coachNotes: OPTIMAL LOAD RULE, THE GOVERNING GATE FROM 24 AUG: a session passes only if it produces no symptoms during it, none immediately after, and none the next day. Any one of the three is a fail, and the next session drops back to the last level that passed. The ceiling during a run is 2/10 with no spike afterwards; mild is allowed, new or worsening is not. This replaces every softer wording elsewhere in this plan. GAIT, MEASURED FROM THE 22 AUG CADENCE STREAM ON 24 AUG. Your descent cadence is already good and is NOT the problem: 177 spm on grades steeper than -20%, 179 spm across the second half of the sustained descents, 176 on the final descent to the door. Do not change it, and do not let anyone tell you to. THE EXPOSURE IS FLAT AND SHALLOW DOWNHILL: 152 spm on flat ground and 156 spm at -3 to -10%. That is precisely the gradient band where the knee spends longest inside the 20-30 degree compression zone under load, it is the running you do most of, and the final 1250m into Bansko is full of it. TARGET 165-170 spm ON FLAT AND SHALLOW DOWNHILL, a 5-10% lift, which is the range the gait-retraining literature uses. Metronome or a 165 bpm playlist. Shorter steps at the same effort; do not convert it into more pace. STEP WIDTH: run slightly wider than feels natural, not on a tightrope. Narrow step width raises ITB strain and strain rate directly and it is one of the few things you can change inside 19 days. FUELLING, FIXED 24 AUG: 80 g/h from minute one, delivered as one 65g sachet of Enervit Isocarb C2:1 Pro per 500ml bottle per hour (60g carbs, 600mg sodium, isotonic) plus one 40g Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro every second hour. Over 7h45 that is roughly 8 sachets and 4 gels. Both are 2:1 glucose-fructose, which is what makes 80 g/h absorbable; a maltodextrin-only gel cannot be stacked on top without exceeding the glucose ceiling. Carry plain water separately for the high traverse if it is warm, and take 150-250ml with every gel. Nothing here is new on the day: this exact system is rehearsed on 29 August and 5 September. Estimated 7h45 moving from your Erve pace reference + altitude penalty. The race is decided by two disciplines: (1) the opening climb at conversational effort no matter who passes you - 1900m continuous from the gun; (2) the final 1250m descent on 7h legs is the single ITB test of the day: poles, short stride, brake with cadence not quads. Half the course is above 2000m - expect pace to mean nothing, run on effort and HR. Fuel 70-90g carbs/h from minute one. Registration + mandatory medical check FRIDAY 13:00-20:00 in Bansko.
